changes.year1_quote: Our operations and financial results are subject to various risks and uncertainties, including those described below.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Our operations and financial results are subject to various risks and uncertainties, including those described below.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2024 disclosure is a general introductory statement that the company faces multiple risks, rather than a distinct economic risk. Year-2025 continues the same general risk framework through the Item 1A risk-factor disclosures; the underlying general risk disclosure is therefore absorbed into the broader Year-2025 risk-factor section rather than meaningfully removed or changed.
changes.title: Risk Factors General Introduction

changes.year1_quote: We may not sustain our growth rate, and we may not be able to manage future growth effectively.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We may not sustain our growth rate, and we may not be able to manage future growth effectively.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 retains the same underlying economic risks: future growth may slow, and the company may fail to manage expansion effectively. The added 2025 revenue figure and minor wording changes do not alter the substance of the disclosure.
changes.title: Growth Rate and Growth Management

changes.year1_quote: We have a history of generating net losses, and if we are unable to achieve adequate revenue growth while our expenses increase, we may not maintain profitability in the future.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We have a limited history of generating net income, and if we are unable to achieve adequate revenue growth while our expenses increase, we may not maintain profitability in the future.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 continues to address the same underlying risk that inadequate revenue growth may not offset rising expenses, resulting in an inability to maintain profitability. However, the disclosure shifts from a history of generating net losses to a limited history of generating net income and reports 2025 net income, weakening the presentation of the historical-loss risk while retaining the future-profitability warning.
changes.title: Net Losses and Future Profitability

changes.year1_quote: We have a limited operating history, and we may have difficulty accurately predicting our future revenue for the purpose of appropriately budgeting and adjusting our expenses.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We have rapidly grown as a business in dynamic and rapidly evolving markets, and we may have difficulty accurately predicting our future revenue for the purpose of appropriately budgeting and adjusting our expenses.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 preserves the same underlying economic risk: difficulty forecasting revenue accurately, which may cause budgeting, cash-flow, operating-result, profitability, and stock-price impacts. The reference to a limited operating history is replaced with rapid growth, but the core forecasting and budgeting risk remains materially unchanged.
changes.title: Limited Operating History and Forecasting

changes.year1_quote: We may be unsuccessful in anticipating and responding to new market trends and evolving industry standards, developing and selling new products, or penetrating new markets.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We may be unsuccessful in anticipating and responding to new market trends and evolving industry standards, developing and selling new products, or penetrating new markets.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 retains the same underlying economic risks: failure to anticipate technology and market changes, develop and sell new products, and penetrate new markets. It also preserves the associated revenue, competitiveness, and industry-standard conformity consequences; the additional discussion expands rather than changes the risk.
changes.title: Product Development and Market Penetration

changes.year1_quote: A substantial portion of our revenue is driven by a limited number of our end customers, and the loss of, or a significant reduction in, demand from one or a few of our top end customers would adversely affect our operations and financial condition.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: A substantial portion of our revenue is driven by a limited number of our end customers, and the loss of, or a significant reduction in, demand from one or a few of our top end customers would adversely affect our operations and financial condition.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 directly retains the same economic risk: substantial revenue concentration among a limited number of end customers and adverse effects from losing a top customer or experiencing reduced demand. The 2025 concentration figures are more severe, but they do not weaken or remove the disclosure.
changes.title: End Customer Concentration

changes.year1_quote: If we fail to achieve design wins for our products, we may lose the opportunity for sales to customers for a significant period of time and be unable to recoup our investments in our products.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: If we fail to achieve design wins for our products, we may lose the opportunity for sales to customers for a significant period of time and be unable to recoup our investments in our products.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 retains the same economic risk: failure to secure design wins can forfeit customer-system sales for an extended period and prevent recovery of product-development investments. It also preserves the related risks of delayed volume shipments, uncertain demand, excess inventory, and adverse operating results; the additional material does not change that treatment.
changes.title: Product Design Wins and Sales Timing

changes.year1_quote: The adoption, use, and commercialization of AI technology, and the continued rapid pace of developments in the AI field, are inherently uncertain.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: The adoption, use, and commercialization of AI technology, and the continued rapid pace of developments in the AI field, are inherently uncertain.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 reproduces the Year-2024 disclosure and preserves the same economic risks: uncertain AI adoption, changing infrastructure requirements, evolving customer needs, and potentially unsuccessful or costly product development. The disclosure is therefore retained in Item 1A.
changes.title: AI Adoption and Infrastructure Requirements

changes.year1_quote: We operate an outsourced manufacturing business model. We currently partner with TSMC to manufacture our integrated circuits. TSMC is our sole manufacturing partner for our integrated circuits and we currently have not qualified another source.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We operate an outsourced manufacturing business model. We currently partner with TSMC to manufacture our integrated circuits. TSMC is our sole manufacturing partner for our integrated circuits and we currently have not qualified another source.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 reproduces the same economic risk in full: reliance on a limited set of third-party manufacturers, including sole-source dependence on TSMC, and the resulting supply, capacity, quality, pricing, and fulfillment risks. The disclosure is materially unchanged rather than merely absorbed into a broader risk.
changes.title: Third-Party Manufacturing Dependence

changes.year1_quote: We are exposed to market risks in the ordinary course of our business. Market risk represents the risk of loss that may impact our financial position due to adverse changes in financial market prices and rates. Our market risk exposure is primarily the result of fluctuations in interest rates and foreign currency exchange rates.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We are exposed to market risks in the ordinary course of our business. Market risk represents the risk of loss that may impact our financial position due to adverse changes in financial market prices and rates. Our market risk exposure is primarily the result of fluctuations in interest rates and foreign currency exchange rates.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 Candidate 1 reproduces the same economic disclosure: exposure to market risk arising primarily from interest-rate and foreign-currency fluctuations. The risk is therefore retained without a material change in substance.
changes.title: Market Risk Exposure Overview

changes.year1_quote: As of December 31, 2024, we had cash and cash equivalents of $79.6 million and marketable securities of $834.8 million, which consisted of cash held in sweep accounts, checking accounts, money market funds, U.S. treasury and agency securities, commercial paper, corporate debt securities, foreign government bonds, and asset-backed securities.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: As of December 31, 2025, we had cash and cash equivalents of $167.6 million and marketable securities of $1,021.2 million, which consisted of cash held in sweep accounts, checking accounts, money market funds, U.S. treasury and agency securities, commercial paper, and corporate debt securities.
changes.reasoning: The disclosure was retained in substance, but the Year-2 investment composition omits foreign government bonds and asset-backed securities, narrowing the stated exposure set. Because the underlying balances and remaining instruments are still disclosed, this is best classified as softened rather than removed.
changes.title: Interest Rate Investment Balances

changes.year1_quote: Due to the short-term nature of our investments, we have not been exposed to, nor do we anticipate being exposed to, material risks due to changes in interest rates.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Due to the short-term nature of our investments, we have not been exposed to, nor do we anticipate being exposed to, material risks due to changes in interest rates.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 retains the same economic disclosure: short-term investments are not expected to create material interest-rate risk, along with the same investment-policy and sensitivity framework. The updated dollar amounts reflect the new reporting year but do not change the risk characterization.
changes.title: Interest Rate Risk Sensitivity

changes.year1_quote: Our reporting currency and the functional currency of our wholly owned foreign subsidiaries in Taiwan, Canada, China, India, and Israel is the U.S. dollar. All of our sales and operating expenses are transacted in U.S. dollars, and therefore our revenue and expenses are not currently subject to significant foreign currency risk.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Our reporting currency and the functional currency of our wholly owned foreign subsidiaries is the U.S. dollar. All of our sales and the majority of our operating expenses are transacted in U.S. dollars, and therefore our revenue and expenses are not currently subject to significant foreign currency risk.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 addresses the same foreign-currency exposure, hedging status, historical gains and losses, and 100-basis-point sensitivity. The change from all operating expenses to the majority of operating expenses and the omission of subsidiary locations do not materially change the disclosed economic risk, so this is a rewording rather than a softening.
changes.title: Foreign Currency Exchange Risk
